programme.title: Foodwise: Xi'an
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Xi'an, an ancient city with over 3000 years of history, capital to 13 Chinese dynasties. But first, our hosts are going to carb load on street food, from glutinous rice cakes and cakes made out of persimmons, to mutton soup with flatbread and the famous biangbiang noodles. They'll also taste the rich history of Xi'an by experiencing a Qin Dynasty-inspired banquet, and try millennia-old dishes such as trout grilled on a ceramic tile and calabash chicken, a Tang Dynasty delicacy. From the Terracotta Army to the Daming Palace, residence of the Tang emperors, to a dazzling nighttime boulevard that recreates the grandeur of the Tang Dynasty, there's so much to explore in Xi'an. So, get your camera and your stomach ready for CGTN's Foodwise in Xi'an!

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill. Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge between history and the present.

programme.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programme.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.

programme.title: The Yak and the Nomad
programme.desc: Qinghai’s Yushu Prefecture is one of China’s key yak-producing regions. This trip took us to Nangqian County, where we explored the yak industry that lies at the heart of Tibetan herders’ daily lives. Trekking into the far-flung pastoral corners of the plateau, we listened closely to the stories behind the hurdles and hopes of pastoral life and development.

programme.title: Painting beyond the spectrum
programme.desc: In many ways, 12-year-old Zhu Jingxiu is just like any other boy his age. He is skilled in drawing, enjoys playing the piano, loves to ride his bicycle, and likes to use his mobile phone to film videos of traffic and skyscrapers.

programme.title: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing
programme.desc: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing delves into the historical origins and cultural background of Fengdu Ghost City, and also features the Zhongyuan Festival celebrations and ancestor-worshipping rituals held here. These activities reflect the local people’s positive and optimistic outlook on life and death, as well as the great importance they attach to their ancestors, families and family traditions.

programme.title: Wujiang: The Land of Silk
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Wujiang District of Suzhou City on China’s east coast to explore the birthplace of silk. There we discover that silk is not merely a precious fabric but also a way of life. For centuries, Wujiang District has been one of China’s largest‑scale silk‑producing regions, which has turned it into a major commercial hub. Local residents worship a distinctive deity‑the Silkworm Goddess. Per the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, the Lesser Fullness of Grain (Xiaoman) solar term coincides with the goddess’s birthday. Local folk opera troupes take turns staging performances on the stage by the main temple hall over several days to mark the occasion and pray for good fortune. We then learn how silk was manufactured centuries ago, before seeing how imperial‑grade silk is being reinvented for modern‑day fashion.

programme.title: Aerial China: Beijing
programme.desc: China’s capital of Beijing is a bucket list city for any self-styled world traveler, but let’s be honest, not all of us have the time! Not to worry, because we’re about to embark on an aerial journey over the nation’s heart, giving you a crash course on this massive hub of culture, international exchange, and technological innovation. If you’re afraid of heights, this may be the one time it’s okay to look down!

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition. From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique “kung fu platform” that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin’s integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates. Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training hard for the arena. Together, their stories reveal Shaolin kung fu’s enduring pull, one that crosses cultures and borders while uniting practitioners through tradition, discipline, and self-mastery.

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: An Encounter with China’s Endangered Monkeys
programme.desc: In this episode, we head to Baima Snow Mountain Nature Reserve in Diqing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, to learn about and participate in the conservation work for the rare and precious national treasure: the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. The presenter ventures into the forest, experiences the daily life of local forest rangers, and witnesses the harmonious relationship between humans and monkeys. We interview "the Monkey Father"—Long Yongcheng, chief scientist of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) and leader of China's Primate Expert Group—who shares stories about the two decades of efforts dedicated to protecting the Yunnan snub-nosed monkey. We also go to the mountains to conduct research alongside young volunteers. Through these activities, we recognize the importance of environmental education for young people in promoting natural ecological balance and harmonious development.

programme.title: 240-Hour Pass in China: Where Pavilions Meet Peaks
programme.desc: Meaning "south of the lake" and "north of the lake," the provinces of Hunan and Hubei in central China take their names from their positions around Dongting Lake – China's second-largest freshwater lake. Nestled along the middle reaches of the Yangtze River, these two provinces are blessed with stunning landscapes and rich local traditions. From the legendary Yellow Crane Tower in Hubei to the breathtaking peaks of Zhangjiajie in Hunan, this journey through central China promises beauty, culture and adventure at every turn. Join CGTN reporter Lucy Lü as she steps into ancient pavilions, uncovers treasured relics, climbs soaring mountains and wanders through riverside towns where tradition and nature come alive in our latest episode of 240-Hour Pass in China: Where Pavilions Meet Peaks!

programme.title: Sanxingdui: Rediscovering a Lost Civilisation
programme.desc: Sanxingdui Site is located at Guanghan, Sichuan Province. It is a site of an ancient city, ancient kingdom and ancient Shu culture in southwest of China, which is the largest in area, longest in time span and richest in cultural connotation. The total area covers 12 square kilometers, which was built over 3000 years ago. The cultural relics at Sanxingdui are precious cultural heritage of mankind, which contain rich historical, cultural and scientific value, and bespeak themselves as the most attractive ones amongst the multitude of the spectacular relics in China. In this episode, under the guide of the presenter, we visit the Sanxingdui Site Garden, archaeological Site and Sanxingdui Museum, show the amazing giant bronze mask, exquisite gold stuff, marvelous bronze divine tree etc., re-explore this mysterious and great civilization 3000 years ago.

programme.title: Escape to Yibin
programme.desc: Yibin is hailed as "The First City along the Yangtze River", home to renowned Yibin Ranmian noodles and Wuliangye liquor. We explored plenty of lesser-known scenic spots: Lizhuang, the cultural hub during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression; vast bamboo groves that embody the hermit culture of China; and the mysterious cliff-hanging coffins. It is precisely these secluded and strategically advantageous lands that enabled local cultures to be well preserved amid turbulent times.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China : Shanghai
programme.desc: Balancing delicately on an alluvial plain and the Yangtze estuary of China’s east coast, much of Shanghai-literally meaning “on the sea”-sits at an average sea-level elevation of about 4 meters. Bisecting the city is the Huangpu River, dividing it into Puxi (west bank) and Pudong (east bank), where you’ll find its famous international airport. Join us as on an aerial cruise as we journey upstream towards one of the world’s most recognizable skylines.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programme.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique “kung fu platform” that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin’s integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates. Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training hard for the arena. Together, their stories reveal Shaolin kung fu’s enduring pull, one that crosses cultures and borders while uniting practitioners through tradition, discipline, and self-mastery.

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition. From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. programme.title: Foodwise: Chongqing
programme.desc: Welcome to Chongqing, China's largest city. Located in the country's southwest, it straddles two mighty rivers and is famed for its extraordinary skyline, with high-rises mushrooming out of the hills and vertigo-inducing bridges.But Tianran He and Angela Fu are here for the food: From xiaomian noodles and Jianghu cuisine to the city's most famous dish: Chongqing hotpot, our hosts take on the spicy, numbing and scintillating aromas of Chongqing cuisine. We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programme.title: Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-4 Medieval Combat
programme.desc: Episode 4 centres on Shanghai, where Eastern and Western martial traditions meet in surprising ways. Kleber visits local practitioners of Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA), trying German and Italian longsword techniques first-hand and seeing how Chinese enthusiasts innovate by combining European swordsmanship with ancient Chinese military manuals. The episode also follows the rise of BUHURT, a European-style armored combat sport now gaining traction in China, featuring locally made traditional Chinese armour in intense full-contact bouts. Through Kleber’s own multicultural martial arts studio and the city’s everyday East-West blend, the episode shows Shanghai as a global hub, a place where classical martial arts find new life and cross-cultural practices thrive.

programme.title: China Untapped: Suzhou
programme.desc: CGTN’s integrated media cultural and travel program "China Untapped: Suzhou" features industrial tourism as its core theme, complemented by Jiangnan cultural tourism. The show follows a narrative thread of a foreign host touring the city alongside an international business investor. Serving as an explorer and guide, host Alex McCutcheon leads the entire industrial tour across Suzhou. UK businessman Athan Fox, acting as a potential investor and observer, views the city through the lens of commercial inspection and identifies the core strengths and investment potential of Suzhou’s high-end manufacturing sector. The production team traveled across Suzhou’s urban districts, Taicang, Kunshan, Changshu and other areas, visiting over 30 enterprises, research institutions and cultural tourism sites. The program presents a perfect blend of robust industrial strength and the exquisite aesthetics of Jiangnan. The two perspectives complement and validate each other, enabling global audiences to learn about Suzhou’s industrial achievements and unique charm in a way that resonates with their cognitive habits.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: Beijing Unboxed: More Than Palaces
programme.desc: When you think of Beijing, what comes to mind? The Forbidden City, the Summer Palace, the Great Wall, the Temple of Heaven? These iconic landmarks tell the story of a city with over 3,000 years of history. But Beijing isn't just about the past. It's a vibrant, ever-changing metropolis. Join travel vloggers Lucy and Ioana as they skip the usual tourist spots and show you a side of Beijing where history, modern life, and creativity meet.

programme.title: The Spirit of Zhaxidele
programme.desc: In this episode of Travelogue, Tianran backpacks the way to the western reaches of China. Making his home in beautiful Jiaju village, he learns just what it takes to be a Tibetan, then reaches the mysterious village of Suopo and explore its ancient watchtowers.

programme.title: China Highly Recommended: Changsha
programme.desc: Episode 1 of Travelogue's "China Highly Recommended" tells the story of Changsha, one of China's happiest cities. Following the lives of four of its foreign residents: A French executive chef, a Japanese podcaster, and two American teachers, we discover the reasons why they made Changsha their second home, and explore the city with them as only locals do. This episode will be released as a 30 minute travel documentary to be broadcast on CGTN's television channel and social media platform, along with a series of video clips and photos

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.1
programme.desc: When Zhejiang's winding river meets the sea it encounters a coastal region studded with islands. On this journey we survey a land of bays, bridges and harbors that is a glorious archipelago of memory, history and culture...

programme.title: Beijing Unboxed: More Than Palaces
programme.desc: When you think of Beijing, what comes to mind? The Forbidden City, the Summer Palace, the Great Wall, the Temple of Heaven? These iconic landmarks tell the story of a city with over 3,000 years of history. But Beijing isn't just about the past. It's a vibrant, ever-changing metropolis. Join travel vloggers Lucy and Ioana as they skip the usual tourist spots and show you a side of Beijing where history, modern life, and creativity meet.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-4 Medieval Combat
programme.desc: Episode 4 centres on Shanghai, where Eastern and Western martial traditions meet in surprising ways. Kleber visits local practitioners of Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA), trying German and Italian longsword techniques first-hand and seeing how Chinese enthusiasts innovate by combining European swordsmanship with ancient Chinese military manuals. The episode also follows the rise of BUHURT, a European-style armored combat sport now gaining traction in China, featuring locally made traditional Chinese armour in intense full-contact bouts. Through Kleber’s own multicultural martial arts studio and the city’s everyday East-West blend, the episode shows Shanghai as a global hub, a place where classical martial arts find new life and cross-cultural practices thrive.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chongqing
programme.desc: Welcome to Chongqing, China's largest city. Located in the country's southwest, it straddles two mighty rivers and is famed for its extraordinary skyline, with high-rises mushrooming out of the hills and vertigo-inducing bridges.But Tianran He and Angela Fu are here for the food: From xiaomian noodles and Jianghu cuisine to the city's most famous dish: Chongqing hotpot, our hosts take on the spicy, numbing and scintillating aromas of Chongqing cuisine. We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programme.title: Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programme.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-4 Medieval Combat

Through Kleber’s own multicultural martial arts studio and the city’s everyday East-West blend, the episode shows Shanghai as a global hub, a place where classical martial arts find new life and cross-cultural practices thrive.

programme.title: China Untapped: Suzhou
programme.desc: CGTN’s integrated media cultural and travel program "China Untapped: Suzhou" features industrial tourism as its core theme, complemented by Jiangnan cultural tourism. The show follows a narrative thread of a foreign host touring the city alongside an international business investor. Serving as an explorer and guide, host Alex McCutcheon leads the entire industrial tour across Suzhou. UK businessman Athan Fox, acting as a potential investor and observer, views the city through the lens of commercial inspection and identifies the core strengths and investment potential of Suzhou’s high-end manufacturing sector. The production team traveled across Suzhou’s urban districts, Taicang, Kunshan, Changshu and other areas, visiting over 30 enterprises, research institutions and cultural tourism sites. The program presents a perfect blend of robust industrial strength and the exquisite aesthetics of Jiangnan. The two perspectives complement and validate each other, enabling global audiences to learn about Suzhou’s industrial achievements and unique charm in a way that resonates with their cognitive habits.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune!

programme.title: Foodwise: Great Walls of Beijing
programme.desc: The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist destination, but did you know that in Beijing, it's where locals go to unwind? From feasts of tofu made using well-water and fish caught fresh from the reservoir, to bubbling cauldrons of thinly-sliced lamb, the hilly suburbs of Beijing are home to some of the city's best-loved weekend escapes - and they're all by the foot of the Great Wall.

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? In this episode, hosts Tianran and Eva will give you a crash course on everything from deciphering the menu and choosing the right restaurant, to pairing dishes according to color, aroma, taste, and form, so that by the end of the show, you too can feast your friends like a pro.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programme.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history. Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode shows how true inner strength is like traditional timber architecture: stable, balanced, and built from within.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.2
programme.desc: Tianran He explores Lhasa’s bustling Barkhor Street, where pilgrims, locals, and visitors alike circle its ancient lanes. This multicultural district, home to sacred temples and boutique shops, becomes the backdrop as Tianran dons traditional Tibetan attire for a photoshoot. Across the city, he meets high school students dancing for Douyin — China’s version of TikTok, blending street dance with traditional Tibetan moves. Finally, Tianran travels to the birthplace of Tibetan incense, where waterwheels still power this thousand-year-old craft.

programme.title: As Chill as the Pandas in Sichuan
programme.desc: Why are pandas so chill? CGTN's Ioana heads to Sichuan to find out, embarking on a journey that's as bashi (effortlessly satisfying) as it is unforgettable. The documentary "As Chill as the Pandas in Sichuan" invites you to slow down, tune in, and discover what it truly means to live a bashi life.

programme.title: Life in the Cloud
programme.desc: The second episode faithfully records what Tianran sees and feels during the backpacking tour in Danba County, Garze Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province. The perseverance, sincerity and hospitality of the people in Xizang leave a profound impression on the travelers visiting this land.

The documentary "As Chill as the Pandas in Sichuan" invites you to slow down, tune in, and discover what it truly means to live a bashi life.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programme.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history. Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode shows how true inner strength is like traditional timber architecture: stable, balanced, and built from within.

programme.title: Foodwise: Great Walls of Beijing
programme.desc: The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist destination, but did you know that in Beijing, it's where locals go to unwind? From feasts of tofu made using well-water and fish caught fresh from the reservoir, to bubbling cauldrons of thinly-sliced lamb, the hilly suburbs of Beijing are home to some of the city's best-loved weekend escapes - and they're all by the foot of the Great Wall.

programme.title: Foodwise: How to Order Chinese Food
programme.desc: How do you order Chinese food? What's the best way to pair dishes? And what's up with the naming system? In this episode, hosts Tianran and Eva will give you a crash course on everything from deciphering the menu and choosing the right restaurant, to pairing dishes according to color, aroma, taste, and form, so that by the end of the show, you too can feast your friends like a pro.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.2
programme.desc: Tianran He explores Lhasa’s bustling Barkhor Street, where pilgrims, locals, and visitors alike circle its ancient lanes. This multicultural district, home to sacred temples and boutique shops, becomes the backdrop as Tianran dons traditional Tibetan attire for a photoshoot. Across the city, he meets high school students dancing for Douyin — China’s version of TikTok, blending street dance with traditional Tibetan moves. Finally, Tianran travels to the birthplace of Tibetan incense, where waterwheels still power this thousand-year-old craft.

programme.title: As Chill as the Pandas in Sichuan

programme.title: Life in the Cloud
programme.desc: The second episode faithfully records what Tianran sees and feels during the backpacking tour in Danba County, Garze Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Sichuan Province. The perseverance, sincerity and hospitality of the people in Xizang leave a profound impression on the travelers visiting this land.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 1
programme.desc: Nanjing, an ancient city that served as the capital of six imperial dynasties, stands as a testament to China's long-standing history and rich culture. From its Porcelain Tower - one of the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages, to its grand city walls and ancient palaces, join us on a voyage across time to experience the echoes of history in Nanjing's storied bricks.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.2
programme.desc: Sichuan's western mountains are a shield safeguarding a true national treasure: the Chengdu Plain, China's very own land of plenty. Join us as we dive from high plateaus into deep gorges, scale snow peaks, and follow rivers in pursuit of an engineering marvel bequeathed by the ancients...

programme.title: Foodwise: Eat Like Confucius
programme.desc: "Foodwise" host Tianran He explores the ancient town of Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius. Together with a 75th generation descendant of the sage himself, they explore one of Confucius' lifelong pursuits: To cultivate oneself for the betterment of others. From the sophisticated cooking techniques and dining etiquette of Confucian cuisine, which was used for banqueting emperors and aristocrats, to getting hands on with street food and local delicacies, Tianran explores how Confucius' ideals have permeated through modern day life in Qufu.

programme.title: Foodwise: The Herbal Way of Life
programme.desc: 'Medicine tonic is not as good as food tonic' - this Chinese saying is a core principle of Traditional Chinese Medicine. It is believed that the right diet and nourishment can cure and reverse the effects of disease, hence considered an inevitable source of natural health preservation. In this Foodwise episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May explore this ancient concept of medicine food homology as they taste their way through different herbs, chat to experts of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and visit venues that combine conventional principles with modern ideas. Dive deep into the origin of TCM with us as we learn about the harmony between man and nature and its application in modern functional foods!

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-6 Shandong Mantis Style
programme.desc: The final episode traces the cross-ocean transmission of Shandong Mantis Style. In the mountains of northern Italy, host Kleber visits Dante Basili, a veteran Italian practitioner in his sixties, who recounts travelling to China 36 years ago to learn Mantis Style and returning home to teach Chinese martial arts ever since. Kleber then heads to Shandong to meet Yu Bo and Yu Tao, sons of Mantis Style grandmaster Yu Hai. He witnesses a traditional apprenticeship ceremony and explores the style’s fighting essence: adopting its spirit rather than merely copying its form. The episode shows how Mantis Style has taken root and flourished in different cultural settings. Ultimately, this journey across Europe and Asia suggests that transmission is not only about techniques, but also about dialogue across time and distance, and a shared resonance of spirit between cultures.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji’s countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.3
programme.desc: Join Tianran He on a high-speed train to Shigatse, gateway to the Himalayas and home to Mount Qomolangma, the world’s highest peak. As the city with the most land ports in Xizang, Shigatse serves as a key corridor to South Asia. Here, Tianran samples breakfast at a bustling local teahouse and experiences monastic life at the vast Tashilunpo Monastery. He then visits an agricultural park where tropical crops thrive against the odds of the alpine plateau, before discovering pulu — a traditional Tibetan textile now earning global acclaim.

programme.title: Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World
programme.desc: When people hear "Spring Festival," they often think of fireworks, red lanterns, and lion dances in the streets. But today, these traditions have grown beyond merely a once-a-year celebration, weaving themselves into people's daily lives across China. The documentary "Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World" embarks on a cultural journey across the nation, tracing how ancient Chinese traditions continue to evolve and engage people worldwide.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 2
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the grand old mansions of Nanjing’s merchant families and take a stroll through their exquisite gardens, where Nature is incorporated into the architecture. From centuries-old Qing Dynasty residences to traditional folk handicrafts, join us on a deep dive into Nanjing’s rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World
programme.desc: When people hear "Spring Festival," they often think of fireworks, red lanterns, and lion dances in the streets. But today, these traditions have grown beyond merely a once-a-year celebration, weaving themselves into people's daily lives across China. The documentary "Spring Festival, a Celebration Shared with the World" embarks on a cultural journey across the nation, tracing how ancient Chinese traditions continue to evolve and engage people worldwide.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-6 Shandong Mantis Style
programme.desc: The final episode traces the cross-ocean transmission of Shandong Mantis Style. In the mountains of northern Italy, host Kleber visits Dante Basili, a veteran Italian practitioner in his sixties, who recounts travelling to China 36 years ago to learn Mantis Style and returning home to teach Chinese martial arts ever since. Kleber then heads to Shandong to meet Yu Bo and Yu Tao, sons of Mantis Style grandmaster Yu Hai. He witnesses a traditional apprenticeship ceremony and explores the style’s fighting essence: adopting its spirit rather than merely copying its form. The episode shows how Mantis Style has taken root and flourished in different cultural settings. Ultimately, this journey across Europe and Asia suggests that transmission is not only about techniques, but also about dialogue across time and distance, and a shared resonance of spirit between cultures.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xilingol
programme.desc: The Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region is located in the northern part of China, stretching from northeast to southwest side. In Xilin Gol, the horses, sheep and cows could be found every where. The local cuisines here are so attractive to the tourists, such as the roasted lamb is a traditional local dish. And the fired stone fried lamb is so hard to find if you are not traveling to Inner Mongolia. Have you ever tried salted milk tea? Just join in this visual trip！

programme.title: Foodwise: Kunming
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in Kunming, the capital of Yunnan province in southwest China. Named the Spring City for its perennially good weather, Kunming is one of China's most ethnically diverse cities, something that's reflected in its food: From boozy sticky rice for breakfast, to the famous "Crossing the Bridge" rice noodles, and evening barbecues, there's plenty on offer here. Also, it's mushroom season, and Tianran is taking to the hills to hunt for wild fungi – but he'll need a trusty friend to steer him away from the poisonous ones!

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

programme.title: A Datong You Don't Know
programme.desc: Datong sits in the northernmost part of Shanxi Province, boasting abundant tourist resources and a long-standing history. This episode of our Buddhist cultural journey centers on the Yungang Grottoes. Following the host’s itinerary with the camera, we’ll show you a lesser-known side of Datong.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art
programme.desc: The documentary "Poet of the Sky: The Liuyang Fireworks Art" follows a heritage master and a visionary show director as they carry a thousand-year-old craft into the future. Originating in Liuyang City, Hunan Province, Liuyang fireworks have evolved from ritual folk traditions into a modern art form that integrates cutting-edge technology. Check out how Liuyang fireworks paint stories across the sky.

programme.title: Exploring Beijing’s Backyard
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the beautiful scenery of Beijing suburbs which is usually ignored by the public. The contents include "Mini Three Gorges" Longqing Valley, "Unique Water Great Wall": Huanghuacheng and "Northern Jiangnan" : Gubei Water Town.

programme.title: Korela Fortress Museum, Russia
programme.desc: 4K Documentary on Korela Fortress Museum, RussiaAt 160 km from St. Petersburg, there is a small town in northern Russia: Priozersk. Here, on the picturesque banks of the Vuoksa River's mouth and Lake Ladoga, stands the Korela Fortress Museum. Medieval Korela was the most northwestern city of Russia on the Vuoksa River island and served to protect against the Swedes' attack. The foundation date of the Korela Fortress is considered to be 1310. This Fortress is the only surviving Swedish bastion-type Fortress in Russia, on which unique buildings of 6-8 centuries are located: Lars Torstenson's Round Gate Tower, the Old Arsenal, the Powder Magazine, and the Suvorov Arsenal. Initially, the buildings of the Fortress were wooden, but numerous fires destroyed them. Over three centuries, the defensive structure was rebuilt and fortified many times. In the 15th century, Korela occupied an area of 6 thousand square meters, consisted of hundreds of log houses, and its population was more than 300 people. The people of the city were engaged in agriculture and fishing and also professed Christianity.By the sixteenth century, the Fortress acquired the form that has survived to this day. In the eighteenth century, the defense served as a prison for essential state criminals. The round gate tower of Lars Torstenson, located at the junction of the north-west and south-west curtains, is a Swedish building. The time of its construction dates back to 1583-1585. In plan, the tower has an almost circular shape, slightly elongated in the western and eastern directions. During its existence, the Fortress has changed more than one name. ""Korela"" repeatedly passed from Sweden to Russia and back and later belonged to Finland. Each country called this place differently. The original name ""Korela"" came from the name of a tribe that once lived in this area. It's interesting to know that until 19-century Korela was located on an island washed on both sides by the Vuoksa river. Due to its favorable geographic location, the Fortress was practically impregnable.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: TechDay Digital Light - Digital Future Lighting
programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. In that context, light technology is steadily growing more important and creating a wider range of possibilities and perspectives, from added safety for the driver, to external communication and individualization. Systematic light digitization is making all of this possible. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. The car can be individualized even further through its digital OLED rear lights. The Digital Matrix LED headlights also include three new functions: advanced traffic information, a lane light with direction indicator lights on highways, and an orientation light on country roads. These features not only demonstrate Audi’s “Vorsprung durch Technik,” they also add value.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.desc:
The new GLC is immediately recognisable as a member of the Mercedes-Benz SUV family. Standard equipment includes the AVANTGARDE exterior with Chrome package including chrome window surrounds and a new, chrome-look simulated underguard. This adds striking design features and enhances the unique proportions of the vehicle. One of the defining design highlights of the GLC is the redesigned front end, with headlamps that connect directly to the radiator grille to emphasise the vehicle’s width, and the new radiator grille as part of the standard AVANTGARDE exterior, which now has a chrome surround and a sporty louvre in matt grey with chrome trim. The body design is characterised by a full, spanned surface design enriched with precisely shaped edges in the sides. These emphasise the proportions, accentuate the muscular wheel arches and create a balance between elegance and off-road performance. Wheel arch liners in the vehicle colour are available from the AMG Line upwards for the first time. These accentuate the sportiness of the AMG Line, as optional equipment in conjunction with mixed tyres. Also available as an optional extra are easy-entry running boards and, from the AMG Line upwards, a Night package.

programme.desc:
With the luxury saloon EQS and the sporty executive saloon EQE, Mercedes-Benz has entered a new, all-electric era in the upper market segments as well. The EQS SUV, the third model series with this architecture developed for electric vehicles, will soon follow. The SUV offers plenty of space, comfort and connectivity for up to seven passengers in its avant-garde, luxurious interior. Thanks to powerful electric motors, responsive 4MATIC all-wheel drive and an intelligent OFFROAD driving mode, the EQS SUV is also capable of tackling light terrain with ease.
The new EQS SUV shares the long wheelbase (3210 millimetres) with the EQS Saloon, but is over 20 centimetres higher. The dimensions in detail: 5125/1959/1718 millimetres (length/width/height). The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: TechDay Digital Light - Digital Future Lighting
programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. In that context, light technology is steadily growing more important and creating a wider range of possibilities and perspectives, from added safety for the driver, to external communication and individualization. Systematic light digitization is making all of this possible. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. The car can be individualized even further through its digital OLED rear lights. The Digital Matrix LED headlights also include three new functions: advanced traffic information, a lane light with direction indicator lights on highways, and an orientation light on country roads. These features not only demonstrate Audi’s “Vorsprung durch Technik,” they also add value.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.title: The new Mercedes-Benz GLC AMG Line World Premiere Teaser
programme.desc:
The new GLC is immediately recognisable as a member of the Mercedes-Benz SUV family. Standard equipment includes the AVANTGARDE exterior with Chrome package including chrome window surrounds and a new, chrome-look simulated underguard. This adds striking design features and enhances the unique proportions of the vehicle. One of the defining design highlights of the GLC is the redesigned front end, with headlamps that connect directly to the radiator grille to emphasise the vehicle’s width, and the new radiator grille as part of the standard AVANTGARDE exterior, which now has a chrome surround and a sporty louvre in matt grey with chrome trim. The AMG Line has a radiator grille with Mercedes-Benz pattern.
The body design is characterised by a full, spanned surface design enriched with precisely shaped edges in the sides. These emphasise the proportions, accentuate the muscular wheel arches and create a balance between elegance and off-road performance. Wheel arch liners in the vehicle colour are available from the AMG Line upwards for the first time. These accentuate the sportiness of the AMG Line, as optional equipment in conjunction with mixed tyres. Also available as an optional extra are easy-entry running boards and, from the AMG Line upwards, a Night package.

programme.title: The Mercedes EQS SUV Electric Art Line Driving Video
programme.desc:
With the luxury saloon EQS and the sporty executive saloon EQE, Mercedes-Benz has entered a new, all-electric era in the upper market segments as well. The EQS SUV, the third model series with this architecture developed for electric vehicles, will soon follow. The SUV offers plenty of space, comfort and connectivity for up to seven passengers in its avant-garde, luxurious interior. Thanks to powerful electric motors, responsive 4MATIC all-wheel drive and an intelligent OFFROAD driving mode, the EQS SUV is also capable of tackling light terrain with ease.
The new EQS SUV shares the long wheelbase (3210 millimetres) with the EQS Saloon, but is over 20 centimetres higher. The dimensions in detail: 5125/1959/1718 millimetres (length/width/height). The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: TechDay Digital Light - Digital Future Lighting
programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. In that context, light technology is steadily growing more important and creating a wider range of possibilities and perspectives, from added safety for the driver, to external communication and individualization. Systematic light digitization is making all of this possible. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. The car can be individualized even further through its digital OLED rear lights. The Digital Matrix LED headlights also include three new functions: advanced traffic information, a lane light with direction indicator lights on highways, and an orientation light on country roads. These features not only demonstrate Audi’s “Vorsprung durch Technik,” they also add value.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.title: The new Mercedes-Benz GLC AMG Line World Premiere Teaser
programme.desc:
The new GLC is immediately recognisable as a member of the Mercedes-Benz SUV family. Standard equipment includes the AVANTGARDE exterior with Chrome package including chrome window surrounds and a new, chrome-look simulated underguard. This adds striking design features and enhances the unique proportions of the vehicle. One of the defining design highlights of the GLC is the redesigned front end, with headlamps that connect directly to the radiator grille to emphasise the vehicle’s width, and the new radiator grille as part of the standard AVANTGARDE exterior, which now has a chrome surround and a sporty louvre in matt grey with chrome trim. The AMG Line has a radiator grille with Mercedes-Benz pattern.
The body design is characterised by a full, spanned surface design enriched with precisely shaped edges in the sides. These emphasise the proportions, accentuate the muscular wheel arches and create a balance between elegance and off-road performance. Wheel arch liners in the vehicle colour are available from the AMG Line upwards for the first time. These accentuate the sportiness of the AMG Line, as optional equipment in conjunction with mixed tyres. Also available as an optional extra are easy-entry running boards and, from the AMG Line upwards, a Night package.

programme.title: The Mercedes EQS SUV Electric Art Line Driving Video
programme.desc:
With the luxury saloon EQS and the sporty executive saloon EQE, Mercedes-Benz has entered a new, all-electric era in the upper market segments as well. The EQS SUV, the third model series with this architecture developed for electric vehicles, will soon follow. The SUV offers plenty of space, comfort and connectivity for up to seven passengers in its avant-garde, luxurious interior. Thanks to powerful electric motors, responsive 4MATIC all-wheel drive and an intelligent OFFROAD driving mode, the EQS SUV is also capable of tackling light terrain with ease.
The new EQS SUV shares the long wheelbase (3210 millimetres) with the EQS Saloon, but is over 20 centimetres higher. The dimensions in detail: 5125/1959/1718 millimetres (length/width/height). The interior dimensions benefit from these generous SUV dimensions and from the advantages of the purpose design tailored to the electric platform. The second row of seats can be electrically adjusted as standard. Up to four golf bags fit in the boot. A third row of seats with two additional individual seats and extensive comfort features for all passengers is available as an option.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: TechDay Digital Light - Digital Future Lighting
programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. In that context, light technology is steadily growing more important and creating a wider range of possibilities and perspectives, from added safety for the driver, to external communication and individualization. Systematic light digitization is making all of this possible. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. The car can be individualized even further through its digital OLED rear lights. The Digital Matrix LED headlights also include three new functions: advanced traffic information, a lane light with direction indicator lights on highways, and an orientation light on country roads. These features not only demonstrate Audi’s “Vorsprung durch Technik,” they also add value.

programme.desc: The sixth generation Opel/Vauxhall Astra and third generation Peugeot 308 are both based on the Stellantis EMP2 platform and, unsurprisingly, score very similarly across all four areas of assessment. Both the offset test and the full-width crash test highlighted marginal chest injury protection for average male and small female drivers, and neither car was equipped with a centre airbag for far-side crash protection, a countermeasure which is increasingly common on modern cars. Both cars offer plenty of crash avoidance technology but do not include some of the latest advancements introduced in the market. The cars’ four-star ratings apply also to their PHEV variants.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.
